backup_rule.text: Per source: the newest successful VolSync sync (status.lastSyncTime, latestMoverStatus.result=Successful) or completed CNPG Backup (metadata.creationTimestamp, phase=completed) must be at or after that source's most recent scheduled run and no older than 24 hours at merge time. VolSync: the most recent run is status.nextSyncTime when that is already past, else nextSyncTime minus the schedule's period (spec.trigger.schedule). CNPG: ScheduledBackup status.lastScheduleTime. CNPG startedAt/stoppedAt are not used: some instances stamp local time with Z.
backup_rule.stateful_evidence: A target is stateless only when every read succeeded and none of these holds: a ReplicationSource applied by its Kustomization; VOLSYNC_* substitutions, a volsync component or dependsOn volsync on that Kustomization; a pod or CronJob of the app mounting a PVC (or an ephemeral claim) in the target namespace; a CNPG client entry. State with no matching ReplicationSource is backup-unmatched (a blocker).

change_lock.status: implemented (story 752); the shepherd stands aside while it shows a lane change in progress (phase merging, merged-awaiting-verification or merge-unknown; story 551, run-shepherd.sh shepherd_may_merge); a hand run refuses while it is held
change_lock.note: ConfigMap upgrade-agent/upgrade-change-lock. Free when absent or data.holder is empty; expired when data.expires_at has passed; otherwise held. Every tick run with --write-state takes it (create, or replace at the resourceVersion it read) before the merge step's reads and releases it before it ends. The lease (600s) is shorter than the 15-minute tick, so a crashed tick costs at most the next one. After a live merge it stays held, phase merged-awaiting-verification, for post_merge_lease_seconds (4h): verification is not built (story 553), so the lane merges at most once a night. The lane does not merge with less than min_lease_left_seconds of lease left. An unreadable lock, or a holder with no readable expires_at, fails closed.

settle_gate.note: Story 551 (R6), facts not clocks (Tom's ruling Q-548-04, 2026-11-11). For a lane-A candidate with an immediate cluster effect, target T in its Flux scope (lane-classify.mjs kustomizationsFor + fluxScope: its Kustomizations, their dependsOn chain, their namespaces) and the cluster-wide parts (cluster_wide_targets): F1 no commit between flux_source's revision and main's head changes T's paths, a path of its chain, or a cluster-wide part (directly or through a shared component, R8); more than max_unapplied_commits, a diverged base or an unreadable commit fails closed. F2 each Kustomization of T's chain has applied (not only attempted) the source revision, is Ready at its generation and not reconciling, and the HelmReleases of T's namespaces are settled. F3 no Kustomization or HelmRelease of a cluster-wide part, nor the source, is progressing. An object in Flux's retry loop, Stalled, failed at its current generation and revision, or DependencyNotReady behind a failing dependency is failing, not settling: the baseline gate judges it by scope. F4 at the merge step and after the merging write: no unfinished Job that can merge (night-merge.mjs SHEPHERD_JOBS). Every read fails closed and names what failed.

pr_record.note: Story 549 (OP512 rollout step 3). One comment per open Renovate PR, written and edited in place by the lane's own identity (the haynes-ops-bot app, REST user.login haynes-ops-bot[bot], type Bot; the shepherd's 64 vet markers on record carry the same identity). Its body starts with the marker line, then one fenced JSON block: the record of upgrade-lane-state projected to these fields. A comment by any other author is never read as the record and never edited, whatever it carries. The lane writes only when the content changed (updated and last_attempt.at are left out of the comparison), keeps the oldest of its own records when it finds two or more and edits each newer one into a note without the marker, and stops every GitHub write for the rest of a tick after the first one that fails; a denial (401, or a 403 that is not a rate limit) also sets the durable halt. A failed write is published in a fixed vocabulary (the HTTP class, network, timeout), never GitHub's own text; a record carrying a credential shape, a private network address or an in-cluster name is not written. Written only by a tick run with --write-state, with a token whose permissions include pull_requests:write, after a ledger write at the version the tick read succeeds, and not while paused (read again just before each write).

retry.note: Story 549, facts not clocks (Tom's ruling Q-548-04). A PR whose lane is BLOCKED by a failing required or expected check (class check-failing) gets Renovate's rebase/retry box ticked when, at the moment of the write: the newest run of the failing check on that head failed and nothing on the head is queued or running; the box exists once and is unticked; the PR is open, Renovate's (renovate[bot], id 29139614) from a renovate/ branch of this repository, and every commit is the Renovate app's; the head has not moved and the body has not changed since the read. At most per_head per head, per_pr per PR in window_days, per_tick box writes per tick (a budget, not a wait; up to about 20 a night in theory, so the per-head and per-PR limits bound the total). The cap counts writes, not PRs tried: a PR the facts at the write refuse hands the slot to the next eligible PR, and at most max_preflights_per_tick PRs are read per tick. A github-actions check suite of the head that is not completed (a workflow run queued, waiting, pending, requested or in progress, read with checks:read) refuses the write. A failure on the head that follows a retry (or Renovate clearing the box without a new head) blocks the PR: class check-failing-after-retry. The ledger is data.retry_ledger on upgrade-lane-state (field manager upgrade-night-ledger), written before the box is ticked and again after; each record shows it under retry.

history.note: Story 593. The history of every attempt: ConfigMap upgrade-agent/upgrade-ledger (runtime state, not Flux-managed), written by upgrade-history.mjs after the merge step in every tick run with --write-state, under field manager upgrade-night-history and always at the resourceVersion the tick read (a conflict writes nothing; the next tick derives the same events); when it is missing it is first created empty under upgrade-night-history-init, and a create that finds another writer's data is a conflict. It remembers; nothing reads it before a merge yet (stories 753 and 556). Events are haynes.upgrade-event/v1 (record-format.mjs), one per line without schema and id: observed (first sight, or a new state, lane or class), closed, merged by someone else, revert-merged (a 'Revert "<title>"' PR whose body names a PR of that title), and in live mode the merge step's events. Every item is named by the lane's route (the PR's package table, labels, title and files through fromLaneRecord); a merge goes on the item that was merged, and a PR moved to a newer version first closes its old item. A fact this tick could not read (who closed a PR, say) writes nothing; the next tick reads it again. max_bytes caps the bytes of upgrade-ledger's data (768 KiB of the API server's 1 MiB): the oldest events rotate out, and an item keeps its state in data.items, so a reverted version stays reverted. marker_configmap records that a history exists (created_at, backfilled_at): with the marker present and upgrade-ledger absent or empty the tick writes nothing and logs an ERROR until a person restores the history or deletes the marker. With no backfill marker the tick backfills the merged Renovate pull requests of the last backfill_days days (and the revert candidates), splitting a list that reaches max_search_results, and compares GitHub's own search count with what the history holds (meta.backfill.compare, summary.history). Each later tick catches up from its newest recorded merge less catch_up_margin_hours. Per tick at most max_pr_reads_per_tick per-PR reads, and no read once the tick has run time_budget_seconds (the Job's deadline is 600s): the rest carries over, and the backfill marker waits until it is done. Terminal events (merged, closed) are mirrored to the PR's lane record as terminal, after the open-PR records, at most max_mirrors_per_tick per tick, until the record carries the event (data.items[id].mirrored); an edit only when it changes, never a new comment; a denial halts only the mirrors (meta.mirror_halt). actors: logins (REST form) that are Renovate, the shepherd and a session; any other bot is unknown (not established), its login kept; anyone else a person. Event reasons are cut to max_reason_chars.

verify.note: Story 553, facts not clocks (Tom's ruling Q-548-04). night-verify.mjs, once per tick after the merge step and before the history: for each update the history (upgrade-ledger) holds in merged_unverified or awaiting_pin it reads, read-only, the facts source (Flux's GitRepository revision contains the merge), applied (the target's own Kustomizations applied a revision that contains it and are Ready; chain and appliers settled, as the settle gate reads them), helmreleases (settled, last release deployed), pods (no CrashLoopBackOff or image-pull failure in pods made since the merge), alerts (no critical alert of the target or its chain that started at or after the merge), image (the workloads' containers run the new tag or digest, or the HelmRelease the new chart), rollout (each Deployment, StatefulSet and DaemonSet in the Kustomization and HelmRelease inventories has pods of one template, none terminating, all Ready) and stable (on an earlier tick the rollout was complete and its pods were recorded; on a later tick the same pods are Ready with no higher restart count). An own image whose digest pin Renovate auto-merges is verified through its pin (the first later commit to one of its pins files), and its wait ends on facts: the image build failed, or main had pin_wait_pushes pushes after the build finished and none was the pin (pin-timeout). Verdict: verified, failed, not-yet or cannot-tell; an unreadable fact never passes. Every verdict lists the other changes on main since the merge that reach the target, its chain or a cluster-wide part (night-merge.mjs otherChanges); a failure with one, or with that list unreadable, is cannot-tell-which-change. practice: verdicts on merges the lane did not make, merged at or after the first commit on main that added night-verify.mjs; they go to upgrade-lane-state (data.verify, data.verify_table) and never to the history. write_history_events: the lane's own merges' verdicts become history events (verified, verification-failed, escalated, awaiting-pin) only when true; git ships false. Per tick at most max_items_per_tick items (least recently judged first), one commit-range read of at most max_range_commits commits, and no new item once the tick has run time_budget_seconds. data.verify keeps at most max_items_kept records within max_state_bytes.

night.baseline_rule: Blockers: a NotReady Kustomization that applies the target, is in its dependsOn chain, or targets its namespace; a NotReady HelmRelease in its namespace; a firing critical alert that belongs to the target (alert_scope: in its namespace and resolved to the target or its chain, unresolvable, or naming no workload), and for a cluster-wide target any critical alert with no namespace; Ceph HEALTH_ERR or unknown. Every other NotReady Flux object is reported as a warning, and every alert that did not block is listed with the reason.
night.pause: A non-empty data.pause on ConfigMap upgrade-lane-state stops every tick before any GitHub read: no merge, no lock take, no PR record and no retry (story 549). The PR-write phase and the retry read it again just before they write. The merge step reads it again just before it takes the lock, so a pause set during a tick stops that tick's merge. Verification and reverts already owed for a merge the lane made carry on through a hook (stories 553, 753, 754; not built). suspend: true on the upgrade-night controller stops every tick, owed work included.

cluster_wide_targets.reason: Flux itself, its bootstrap and the apps root (files directly under kubernetes/main/apps, applied by flux-system/cluster-apps, which kubernetes/main/flux/apps.yaml defines): every Kustomization depends on it
Ceph, its operator and its CSI drivers: most volumes
CSI drivers, local volumes, snapshots and VolSync: volumes in every namespace

alert_scope.doc: R5 (OP550). A firing critical alert blocks a lane-A target only when it belongs to the target. Its namespace is the namespace label, else exported_namespace (Flux alerts). An alert in a namespace of the target's dependsOn chain (a chain Kustomization's namespace or targetNamespace) blocks only when it traces to a chain Kustomization; there it is otherwise listed, with no namespace fallback. An alert in any other namespace does not block. Inside the target's namespaces, the first workload label present (subject_labels, in order) names the subject; the tick resolves it against the namespace's pods, Jobs, CronJobs and HelmReleases to the Kustomization that applied it. It blocks when that Kustomization is the target's or in its dependsOn chain, when the label cannot be resolved (fail closed) and when the alert names no workload (namespace fallback). It does not block when the subject resolves to another Kustomization. A pod that is the scraping exporter itself (scraper_pod_app_names) names no workload. An alert with no namespace at all blocks only a cluster-wide target (cluster_wide_targets).
alert_scope.no_namespace: An alert with neither namespace nor exported_namespace blocks every cluster-wide target and no other target. Seen 2026-11-10 and 2026-11-11: DevEnvRescueFailed (session), CNPGBackupStale (job=<ns>/<cluster>), KyvernoEnforceBlockingAdmission (policy_name), GpuMissing and the SMART alerts (node), SigoalumniServiceEndpoints* (service), KubeAPIErrorBudgetBurn, CephOSDDownHigh, PVEExporterNoData.
alert_scope.namespace_fallback_seen: Critical alerts seen in the 30 days to 2026-11-11 that block every target in their namespace because they name no workload or name one the tick cannot trace: BlackboxProbeFailed and AlertmanagerClusterFailedToSendAlerts (observability, no workload label); PersistentVolumeClaimStuckPending (its pod label is kube-state-metrics itself); KubePersistentVolumeFillingUp when no running pod mounts the claim; CephDaemonCrash (rook-ceph) and etcdDatabaseQuotaLowSpace (kube-system), whose pods have no Flux or Helm owner. Traced to an owner, so they block only a target that is that owner or depends on it (checked for the labels on 2026-11-11): MediaAutomationJobFailed and KometaOverlaysRunTooLong (job_name), CigarJournalCredentialMonitorStale (cronjob), QbittorrentVpnDown (deployment), OOMKilled (pod, while that pod exists), the PVE alerts (the exporter pod, prometheus-pve-exporter), NodeRebooted (node-exporter, kube-prometheus-stack), FluxReconciliationFailure for a Kustomization or HelmRelease (exported_namespace and name); a failing Flux source blocks its namespace.

shared_components.doc: R8 (OP550). The kustomization.yaml directories that include each shared component (components:, and through a component that includes another). A changed file maps to the deepest component that contains it; its consumers become the PR's targets and are judged by the path classes and path rules as if the PR had touched them. No entry or no consumer: the component path stays the target, which the tick reports as target-unmapped. scripts/upgrade-agent/lane-classify-selftest.mjs rebuilds this list from the repository and fails when it differs; --print-shared-components prints it.

check_rules.doc: R7 (OP550). Checks are stale when a commit on main that touches one of the PR's files is newer than the head's checks: the earliest of the head commit's date and the start of each expected check's newest attempt (a re-run reuses the old merge commit, so its own start time is not used alone). Read per file with gh api GET repos/<repo>/commits?sha=main&path=<file>&since=<time>. A failed read, or no readable time, blocks (fail closed). The age rule (check_max_age_days) still applies too. lane-classify.mjs exports checksReferenceTime, mainCommitsTouching and checksPredateMain for the merge step (story 752).
check_rules.branch_up_to_date: Off for main, established 2026-11-11 from read-only evidence: PR 3915, 92 commits behind main with both required checks SUCCESS, reads mergeStateStatus CLEAN (with the setting on it would read BEHIND); and #4333, #4340, #4693, #4670 and #4753 were merged on 2026-11-10 by the non-admin haynes-dev-bot while 11 to 80 commits behind main. GET /branches/main/protection is not readable by the bot, so the setting itself was not read.
